3. Transferts vers des fournisseurs IA tiers

Lorsque tu utilises Shreddy (chat) ou un scan IA, ton message ou ta photo est envoyé directement (sans intermédiaire ShredCoach) au fournisseur que tu as choisi. Tu fournis ta propre clé API. Les fournisseurs ont leurs propres politiques :

• Groq (États-Unis) — https://groq.com/privacy-policy
• OpenAI (États-Unis) — https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy
• Anthropic Claude (États-Unis) — https://www.anthropic.com/privacy
• Google Gemini — https://policies.google.com/privacy
• Mistral (France) — https://mistral.ai/terms/

Ces transferts hors UE sont fondés sur l'art. 49.1.a RGPD (consentement explicite). Tu peux refuser : l'app fonctionnera sans ces fonctions.

Si tu actives la sauvegarde, ShredCoach écrit une archive ZIP dans le dossier que TU choisis (Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, local). Le contenu et la sécurité de ce dossier dépendent du fournisseur que tu as sélectionné — leur politique s\'applique à l\'archive. ShredCoach ne lit pas l\'archive après écriture.

• **Accès** : tu peux exporter toutes tes données via Paramètres > Sauvegarde > Sauvegarder maintenant (archive JSON + photos lisibles).

• **Rectification** : tu modifies directement tes données dans l'app.

• **Effacement** : Paramètres > Supprimer toutes mes données. Tout est effacé du téléphone en une opération atomique.

• **Portabilité** : l'archive de sauvegarde est en JSON ouvert + photos JPEG.

• **Opposition / retrait du consentement** : désactive Shreddy ou les scans IA dans les paramètres pour stopper les transferts vers les fournisseurs tiers.

Tes clés API IA sont chiffrées via Android Keystore (AES-256-GCM, hardware-backed sur la majorité des appareils). Le trafic réseau utilise TLS 1.2+. La base de données Room est protégée par le chiffrement disque Android (FBE) si activé sur ton appareil.

Back flat against the seat. Feet centered on the platform, shoulder-width. Descend to at least 90°. NEVER lock your knees at the top.
High feet = glutes, low feet = quads.
Squat rack + Olympic bar (45 lb empty).
Bar on traps. Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Descend until thighs are parallel. Back straight, drive through your heels.
King of all exercises. Minimum 3 sec on the descent.
Big step forward, back knee grazes the ground. Front knee should not go past the toes. Torso upright.
Add dumbbells once it gets too easy.
Leg extension machine. Knees aligned with the rotation axis.
Seated, fully extend your legs. Squeeze the quads for 2 sec at the top. Controlled 3-sec descent.
Perfect finisher after squat or leg press.
Leg curl machine. Lie face-down, ankles under the roller.
Curl your knees toward the glutes. Squeeze for 2 sec at the top. Very slow descent (3 sec). Hips stay glued to the bench.
Most neglected zone. Slow descent is the key.
Standing, bar in front of thighs. Hinge at the hips, pushing the glutes back. Back FLAT. Lower to mid-shins. Stand back up squeezing the glutes.
Excellent for glutes + hamstrings. Flat back is mandatory.
Floor mat. Advanced variant: back on a bench + bar across the hips.
Lying down, knees bent, feet on the floor. Drive the hips toward the ceiling. Squeeze glutes for 2 sec at the top.
Activates the glutes better than the squat. Progress to barbell hip thrust.
Seated leg curl machine. Thighs locked in, ankles on the roller.
Curl knees under the seat. Squeeze for 2 sec. Controlled return.
Hits the hamstrings from a different angle than the lying curl.
Chest press machine (converging or guided). Seated, handles at chest height.
Back flat against the seat. Push the handles forward. Don\'t lock the elbows. Controlled return.
Perfect to start with. Safe, no spotter needed.
Flat bench + bar rack. Olympic bar 45 lb.
Shoulder blades retracted, feet on the floor. Lower the bar to the mid-chest (2 sec). Pause 1 sec. Press up (2 sec). Never bounce.
The king pec exercise. Use a spotter on heavy sets.
Floor. Variants: incline push-ups (hands on bench = easier), decline push-ups (feet on bench = harder).
Hands shoulder-width + 4 in. Body braced. Lower chest to the floor. Push back up to extension. Elbows at 45°.
If 20+ reps feel easy, switch to weighted (backpack) or decline push-ups.
Cable crossover (two facing pulley columns). High or middle handles.
Arms out wide, elbows slightly bent. Bring hands together in an arc in front of you. Squeeze pecs for 2 sec.
Carves the separation between the pecs. Contraction beats heavy load.
Incline chest press machine (if available) or Smith machine + incline bench.
Same movement as the chest press, but at an incline angle. Press up and slightly forward.
Lower dumbbells out to each side, elbows at 45°. Bring them together at the top without clinking.
Complements the bench press for full chest development.
Bench or step to elevate the feet. The higher the feet, the more the upper chest works.
Feet on the bench, hands on the floor. Same execution as standard push-ups.
Advanced push-up variant that targets the upper chest.
Arms open, elbows slightly bent. Lower in an arc. Bring back up while squeezing.
A burning sensation = good sign. Light and precise.
Lat pulldown machine. Thighs locked under the pads. Wide bar.
Pull the bar to the TOP of the chest (never behind the neck). Squeeze the shoulder blades for 2 sec. Torso fixed.
Builds the V-taper. Drive elbows toward your back pockets.
Olympic bar on the floor. Alternative: Smith machine.
Torso at 45°, back FLAT. Pull the bar toward the navel. Elbows travel behind the back. Squeeze shoulder blades 1 sec.
Builds back thickness. Rounded back = too heavy.
Fixed pull-up bar. Use an assisted machine if needed.
Pronated grip (palms forward) wider than the shoulders. Pull until your chin clears the bar. 3-sec descent.
Best back exercise. Use assistance if you can\'t hit 8 reps.
High pulley + straight bar. Standing facing the pulley, slightly bent.
Arms nearly extended, pull the bar in an arc toward the thighs. Squeeze the back at the bottom. Controlled return.
Isolates the lats without biceps. Straight arms = key.
Low pulley with seat. V-handle (close grip).
Pull the handle toward the navel. Squeeze shoulder blades for 2 sec. Torso fixed, don\'t lean back.
Targets the rhomboids (mid-back) and improves posture.
1 dumbbell + flat bench for support (knee + hand).
Knee and hand on the bench, back flat. Pull the dumbbell toward the hip (not the shoulder). Elbow rises high.
Smith bar set at chest height. Or low rack bar.
Under the bar, body straight, feet on the floor. Pull the chest to the bar. Controlled descent.
Beginner version of the pull-up. Excellent for posture.
High pulley + rope. Standing facing the pulley.
Pull the rope toward your face while spreading your hands. Elbows high. Squeeze for 2 sec. End in a double-biceps pose.
Protects the shoulders and builds the rear delts.
Shoulder press machine. Seated, handles at ear level.
Press the handles overhead. Don\'t lock the elbows. Lower back down to ear level.
Dumbbells at ear level, elbows at 90°. Press overhead. Don\'t go below ear level. Abs braced.
Shoulders are fragile — load progressively. No back arch.
Floor. Push-up position with hips raised (inverted V shape).
Lower your head toward the floor by bending the elbows. Push back up. The higher the feet, the harder.
Progression toward the handstand push-up. Excellent for mass.
Light dumbbells or lateral raise machine.
Arms at your sides. Raise to horizontal. Elbows higher than the hands. 3-sec descent.
Builds shoulder width. Think \"elbows to the ceiling\". Light and strict.
Seated curl machine. Elbows on the support pad, supinated grip.
Curl the handles toward your shoulders. Squeeze for 1 sec. Controlled 2-sec descent.
Isolates the biceps perfectly, no cheating possible.
Elbows pinned to the body, FIXED. Curl up to the shoulders. 3-sec descent. Full extension at the bottom.
Pull-up bar. Supinated grip (palms toward you), shoulder-width.
Pull until your chin clears the bar. The biceps work more than in pronation.
Best biceps exercise. Also works the back.
Lying on the bench, arms hanging. Curl by bending the elbows. FULL 3-sec descent.
Builds the biceps peak. The bottom stretch is the key.
High pulley + rope or straight bar.
Facing the pulley, elbows pinned to the ribs. Push down. Spread the rope at the bottom. Squeeze for 1 sec.
Spreading the rope at the bottom recruits the long head (volume).
Lying down, arms extended. Bend the elbows to lower the bar toward the forehead. Elbows FIXED. Press back up.
Builds the triceps horseshoe. Precision movement.
Arms extended, lower until elbows reach 90°. Upright = triceps, leaned forward = pecs. Push back up.
If too hard, use the assisted machine. One of the best upper-body exercises.
Bent over, elbow at 90° against the body. Extend the arm back. Squeeze for 2 sec. Lower back down.
Triceps finisher. Light and controlled, burning sensation.
High pulley + rope. Kneeling facing the pulley.
Rope behind the head. Crunch the sternum toward the pubis. Hips do NOT move. Squeeze for 2 sec, exhale fully.
Best gym ab exercise. Progressively loadable.
Floor mat + weight plate (10–22 lb) held against the chest.
Lying down, knees bent, plate on chest. Crunch the shoulders up. Squeeze for 1 sec. Lower without resting.
Loaded version of the classic crunch. Easy progression.
Lying down, knees bent, hands behind the head (don\'t pull the neck). Crunch the shoulders up. Squeeze for 1 sec.
Basic but effective. 20+ reps with slow contraction.
Ab crunch machine (seated, handles in front).
Crunch the torso down against the resistance. Squeeze for 2 sec. Controlled return.
Guided and safe. Good alternative to the cable crunch.
Torso rotation machine. Seated, handles to the sides.
Rotate the torso side to side against the resistance. Control the movement.
Sculpts the obliques. Slow and controlled, no jerking.
Heavy dumbbell in each hand. Walk 100–130 ft keeping the torso perfectly upright. Abs braced.
Trains the transverse + obliques + forearms. Functional.
Raise the knees toward the chest by CURLING the pelvis. 3-sec descent. Without the curl = useless.
Targets the lower abs (below the navel). The pelvic curl is everything.
Plank: forearms + toes, 45–60 sec. Side plank: on your side, 30 sec/side. Body = straight line.
Strengthens the transverse (flat stomach) + obliques (slim waist).
Standing calf raise machine. Shoulders under the pads, balls of the feet on the edge.
Rise as high as possible on the toes. Squeeze for 2 sec. Lower the heels as far as possible. FULL range of motion.
Calves resist growth. Range of motion + volume = key.
Bar on the traps (squat rack) or dumbbells in hand + step.
Balls of the feet on the step, heels in the air. Raise/lower with maximum range of motion.
Progress to heavy loads. Calves can take a lot.
Stair step. One foot at a time for more intensity.
Ball of the foot on the step, heel in the air. Raise and lower slowly. 20 reps/foot.
One foot at a time doubles the intensity. Hold onto the wall.
Seated calf raise machine. Knees under the pads.
Rise on the toes, squeeze for 2 sec, lower heels low. Knees at 90°.
Targets the soleus (deep muscle). Complements the standing calf raise.
Feet very wide, toes pointed outward. Descend keeping the back straight. Drive through the heels to stand up.
Targets the adductors and glutes more than the classic squat.
Hold the weight against your chest. Squat deep keeping the elbows between the knees. Stand up driving through the heels.
Back foot on the bench. Lower the back knee toward the floor. Keep the torso upright. Drive through the front foot.
Unilateral: corrects imbalances. Stretches the rear-side hip flexor.
Place the bar on the traps. Feet slightly forward. Descend until 90°. Stand up under control.
Safer than free squats, lets you load heavier.
Hold a support. Lean the torso back while bending the knees. Descend keeping the hips aligned.
Extreme quad isolation. Watch out if your knees are sensitive.
Back against the pad. Feet shoulder-width. Squat deep. Drive up to stand.
Guided machine, lets you load heavy safely.
Step onto the bench with one foot. Drive up fully. Step down under control.
Functional unilateral work. Bench height = difficulty.

Advanced exercise requiring strength, balance and mobility.

Feet hip-width. Grip the bar. Flat back, push the floor with your feet. Lock out at the top.

Feet very wide, toes outward. Grip the bar between the legs. Push the floor to stand up.

Legs nearly straight. Lower the bar along the legs while pushing the hips back. Stand up by contracting the hamstrings.
More hamstring stretch than the Romanian variant.
Bar on the traps. Hinge at the hips pushing the glutes back. Flat back. Stand up squeezing the glutes.

Strap on the ankle. Face the pulley. Push the leg back keeping the back straight.

Set up on the GHR bench. Lower the torso toward the floor. Stand back up by contracting the hamstrings and glutes.
Combines knee flexion and hip extension.
Set the machine. Push the thigh back contracting the glute. Control the return.
Gluteus maximus isolation. Squeeze hard at the top.
Seated, thighs spread on the pads. Squeeze thighs together. Control the return.

Seated, thighs together against the pads. Spread thighs outward. Control the return.

Seated, pull the handle to the hip with one arm. Slight torso rotation. Control the return.

Standing, arms by your sides. Raise one dumbbell in front to shoulder height. Lower slowly.

Seated, dumbbells in front of the face palms in. Press up rotating the wrists to finish palms forward.
Full rotation: trains all 3 deltoid heads.
Handstand position against a wall. Lower the head toward the floor. Press back up.

Back to the pulley. Grab the rope above the head. Extend the arms upward and forward.
Hands on a bench behind, feet on another in front. Lower bending the elbows. Press up.
Easier than classic dips. Add weight on the thighs to progress.
Lying down. Lower the bar toward the chin (between skullcrusher and close-grip press). Press up contracting the triceps.
Lying down. Dumbbells above the chest. Bend the elbows to bring the dumbbells toward the chest, elbows pointing outward. Press back up.

Lying down, knees bent. Bring the torso all the way up to seated. Lower slowly.
Full motion, also recruits the hip flexors.
Lying down, arms and legs extended. Raise torso and legs simultaneously to touch the feet. Form a V.
Trains the entire rectus abdominis simultaneously.
Lying down, hands behind the head. Bring elbow toward opposite knee, alternating. Pedaling motion.
One of the best oblique exercises per EMG studies.
Seated, feet off the floor. Rotate the torso left to right while holding the weight.
Targets the obliques. Reps count each side.
Plank position. Alternately bring the knees to the chest at speed.
Cardio + abs. Keep the hips low and stable.
On the knees. Roll forward extending the body. Return to start by contracting the abs.
Intense exercise. Start on the knees before attempting standing.
Lying on a bench. Hold the end. Raise the entire body like a flag. Lower slowly without touching the bench.
Lying down, legs bent. Roll the hips toward the chest lifting the glutes off the floor. Lower slowly.
Grab the handle up high. Pull diagonally downward while rotating the torso. Control the return.
Functional rotational movement. Trains the obliques.
Lying down, arms and knees at 90°. Extend one arm and the opposite leg simultaneously. Return and alternate.
Excellent for core stability and coordination.
Lying down, arms extended overhead. Lift shoulders and legs off the floor. Hold the position.
Foundational gymnastics position. Reps = seconds of hold.
Standing perpendicular to the pulley. Hold the handle in front of the chest. Extend arms forward without rotating the torso.
Set up on the 45° bench. Lower the torso toward the floor. Stand back up by contracting the lower back and glutes.
Don\'t hyper-extend. Stop at body alignment.
Lying face-down. Raise arms and legs simultaneously. Hold 2–3 seconds. Lower.
Simple but effective for the spinal erectors.
On all fours. Extend one arm and opposite leg simultaneously. Hold 2 seconds. Alternate.
Stability, coordination and lower-back strength. Ideal for rehab.
Grab a heavy dumbbell in each hand. Walk straight for 65–130 ft keeping the shoulders down and core engaged.
Reps = seconds of walking. Builds grip strength, traps and core.
Hang from the bar with extended arms. Hold as long as possible.
Reps = seconds. Builds grip endurance and decompresses the spine.
Forearms on the thighs, wrists hanging off. Curl the wrists upward to lift the bar. Lower slowly.
Short but intense range. Burn guaranteed.
Bent forward, balls of the feet on a step. Rise on the toes. Lower stretching the calves.
Bent-over position stretches the gastrocnemius more.
Feet at the bottom of the platform, balls of the feet on the edge. Push with the toes then lower stretching.
Facing the box. Jump onto the box landing flat-footed. Step down under control.
Plyometric: builds leg and calf power.
Bar on the front delts, elbows high. Descend until thighs parallel keeping the torso vertical. Push through the heels.
More quads, less glutes than back squat. Wrist mobility required.
Back against the pad, feet low on the platform. Squat deep keeping lordosis. Push back up without locking out.
Arc trajectory follows the natural squat path without loading the spine.
Belt squat machine or belt + plates.
Load on the belt (not the spine). Feet shoulder-width. Squat deep. Torso upright, neutral spine.
Completely unloads the spine — ideal if you have lower-back issues.
Standing in the center of the bar. Grab the handles, flat back. Push the floor to stand keeping the torso more vertical than a classic deadlift.
Squat/deadlift hybrid. Safer for the back than classic deadlift.
Seated, back against the pad, feet on the platform. Lower the knees toward the chest. Press to extend the legs.
Seated hack variant — targets quads without lumbar stress.
Feet very wide. Shift weight onto one leg keeping the other straight. Squat deep. Stand and alternate.
Hip mobility + adductors + balance. Excellent for mobility.
Classic squat but briefly sit on the box, then explode up without rebound.
Breaks the stretch reflex — builds pure power from the bottom.
Unloaded squat at a steady pace. Arms extended forward for balance. Descend until thighs parallel.
Classic warm-up — activates the legs and increases circulation.
Hip hinge: push the hips back letting the kettlebell swing between the legs, then snap the hips forward explosively (the KB rises by inertia).
Power = hips, not arms. Top exercise for the posterior chain + cardio.
Bar resting on the supports at knee height. Grip with flat back. Pull pushing the floor and extending the hips.
Reduced range = heavier loads possible. Strengthens deadlift lockout.
Grip the plates (not the bar) with your hands. Pull keeping the back flat. Very technical.
Advanced variant — heavy demand on grip and traps along with posterior chain.
Lying on the floor, bar above the chest. Lower until the elbows touch the floor (no further). Press to lockout.
Reduced range — easier on the shoulders. Ideal for recovery or triceps lockout work.
Lying on a flat bench, legs extended forward (NOT on the floor). Perform a classic bench press without leg drive.
Eliminates leg drive — pure pec isolation. Pure technical strength.
Lying under the Smith. Hold 2 dumbbells together (hexagons pressed). Press while squeezing the pecs.
Constant adduction — intense burn at the center of the pecs.
Standing, press the plate between your palms at chest level. Extend the arms forward keeping the pressure. Return.
Finisher — total congestion of the inner pec.
Grip the bar in supination (palms toward you). Lower slowly, arms close to the body. Press without locking out.
Recruits the clavicular head (upper pecs) more. Spotter needed.
Kneeling facing the landmine. Grab the bar with both hands. Press forward and upward squeezing the upper pecs.
Arc trajectory — spares the shoulders while loading the upper chest.
Elbows at shoulder height, forearms pointing down. Externally rotate to bring the forearms above the head.
Prehab — strengthens the rotator cuff. Light load mandatory.
Standing, pulley on the opposite side. Arm by your side. Raise laterally to shoulder height. Lower slowly.
Constant tension — better mid-delt recruitment than dumbbells.
Standing, bar at shoulder height. Press up and slightly forward. Arc trajectory.
Ideal for sensitive shoulders — less impact than a classic overhead press.
Side to the pulley. Elbow tucked, forearm at 90°. Rotate the forearm outward. Control the return.
KB in rack position (bell against the forearm). Press overhead while stabilizing. Control the descent.
Rack position = recruits core stability. Train unilateral.
Lying face-down on the bench, arms hanging. Pull the dumbbells to the hips squeezing the shoulder blades. Controlled descent.
No cheating possible — no leg drive or torso movement.
Plank position on the dumbbells. Pull one dumbbell to the hip while stabilizing the hips (no rotation). Alternate.
Combines row + anti-rotation plank. Massive for the core.
Torso bent at 45°, flat back. Grip the bar overhand. Pull to the lower sternum. Squeeze the shoulder blades.
Guided trajectory — pure focus on back contraction without stabilization.
Standing facing the pulley, arms extended. Pull the bar toward the thighs keeping the arms straight (slight bend). Movement comes from the lats.
Pure lat isolation — mind-muscle connection critical.
Incline bench + EZ bar or dumbbells.
Lying face-down on an incline bench. Arms hanging. Curl keeping the elbows fixed. Squeeze at the top.
Eliminates cheating — maximum isolation of the short head of the biceps.
Classic supinated curl. At the top, rotate palms downward (pronation). Slow descent in pronation. Rotate at the bottom to repeat.
Hammer grip (palms facing each other). Curl without rotating the wrists. Elbows fixed at the body.
Targets the brachialis and brachioradialis. Adds arm volume (forearms included).
Seated, elbow braced against the inner thigh. Curl squeezing the biceps. Slow descent, full stretch.
Maximum isolation — peak contraction is the highest tested via EMG.
Standing facing the pulley, arms extended. Curl keeping the elbows fixed. Constant tension throughout the rep.
Constant cable tension — better recruitment than a free bar.
On the side, supported on the forearm. Hips aligned with the shoulders. Hold the position. Alternate sides.
Reps = seconds of hold. Targets obliques + quadratus lumborum.
Lower back on the ball, feet on the floor. Crunch by raising the torso. Take advantage of the extended range (pre-stretch on the abs).
Greater range than a floor crunch — better upper-ab stimulation.
Bear plank, knees 1 in off the floor. Extend one leg backward squeezing the glute. Reset and alternate.
Combines plank + hip extension. Anti-rotation core.
Bar on the traps, balls of the feet on the step. Rise on the toes. Lower in a full stretch.
Guided trajectory — heavier loading than dumbbells. Full bottom stretch.
Push the sled over the chosen distance. Torso leaned forward. Explosive steps. Keep the rhythm.
Reps = meters covered. Top conditioning + legs + cardio.
Squat, hands to the floor, throw the legs into a plank, push-up (optional), return to squat, jump with arms overhead. Chain.
Intense full body. Ideal as a finisher or CrossFit-style WOD.
Light hops on the balls of the feet. Elbows close to the body, wrist rotation to spin the rope. Steady rhythm.
Reps = seconds. Cardio + calves + coordination. Perfect warm-up.
Lunge position, back knee on the floor. Push the hips forward keeping the torso upright. Hold 30s.
Reps = seconds per side. Crucial after a sedentary day.
On the rear knee. Grab the back ankle and pull toward the glute. Push the hips forward.
Stretches quadriceps + psoas simultaneously. Ideal post-leg day.
Standing, hands on the hips. Circle the pelvis. 10 in one direction, 10 in the other.
Activates the hips before legs. Do at the start of the session.
